title: Money that earns money
concept: Compound interest: $1,000 at 7% a year for 30 years grows to about $7,612, versus $3,100 with simple interest, because interest earns interest.
kept: guess first, then play year by year, then compare the two stacks at the end
a coin stack that grows every year next to a stack that grows by only $70 a year, so the gap is visible
their simple-interest misconception ($1,000 + 30 x $70 = $3,100) shown as the second stack
rule of 72 (they said they know it)
filled_in: a number guess with feedback compared to the computed total
Next year and Play all 30 years buttons
coins colored by origin (put in, interest both piles get, interest on interest) to make the gap inspectable
per-year note showing the interest each pile earns that year
a 'Why is the gap so big?' step that splits the total into three computed parts
a yearly rate slider (1% to 12%) as the exploration step
rule of 72 note compared with the first year the pile reaches $2,000
small table of piles every 5 years
a model label: fixed yearly rate, no deposits, fees or taxes

changed.what: Their guess of 'around 7,600' is kept as the correct answer but shown as the computed $7,612, not typed in.
changed.why: 1,000 x 1.07^30 = 7,612.26, so 7,600 is a good rounding; every number on screen is calculated by the code.

math_check: Computed independently: 1000 * 1.07^30 = 7612.255; simple = 1000 + 30*70 = 3100; interest on interest = 4512.26; first year at or above $2,000 is year 11 (1.07^10 = 1.967, 1.07^11 = 2.105), against rule of 72 estimate of 10.3 years. Page values are generated by loops, then checked against these with the check script and a manual walkthrough.
